reviews.comment: Physics is about practicing and mastering the material, not expecting to perform well without work outside class. With that being said, Professor Wu explains the material well and does practice problems straight from old exams. Because the old exams are provided to you, this is extremely valuable. His office hours are also very consistent.

Professor Wu's is very kind however lectures aren't really helpful, at some point I stopped attending & studied on my own, exams are equation based and his lecture are more conceptual. The SI sessions saved me, the TA explained the material & went over questions similar to the ones on the exam. Dr.wu posts past exams making studying extremely easy.

Dr. Wu knows the content very well, he is just so so bad at teaching it. His lectures consist of him quickly going over random sample problems that are unlike exam questions. Students walk out of each lecture confused and annoyed. Id avoid him if you can, but if you have to take him, dont even both with lecture, GO TO RECITATION AND SI!!!!

After the first test, attendance dropped from 60 to 15 bc people quickly realized his teaching was useless. Has a heavy accent and does not solve problems the way anyone else does due to his prior knowledge of physics and his unreasonably hard-to-follow shortcuts within the problems. Want to teach yourself Physics 201? Take him. SI IS A LIFESAVER!

Wu has a bad rap, but the class is very manageable. Physics is a hard subject, but he gives you all the materials you need to succeed (14 practice tests per exam). I never did the homework but got 95+ on each exam. Lecture was hard to sit through, but paying attention helped, because he walked you through how to solve exam problems. GO TO S.I.!!

The professor, by all means, knows what he is doing. However, he is just reading from the textbook. Let's just say that I only learned from recitation. And by the end of the semester, only a third of the students were still showing up to class. Find some other way to learn if you have this professor. Tutor, friends, whatever.

Lectures have no flow to them, and no good explanations. He just jumps into old exam problems with no explanations of the concepts. Read the book on your own, and understand the HWs for easy A. Barely anyone attended lecture. At the very least Wu is very nice, caring, and has an awkward humor to him. He is also pretty available outside of class
Be prepared to teach your self
Great guy, super open to questions, preapres you well for exams. Hard class, but do-able if you study, especially old exams.
reviews.ratingTags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Wu does not seem to understand the basic job requirements of his position, Conceptual material was not covered, He would jump into examples with no explanation, often make mistakes in his examples, Unhelpful in answering questions. Often seemed very confused. If you get stuck with him, dont bother going to lecture, Recitations and other profs.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a terrible, terrible professor. 3 mid-terms make up 55% of the grade with the final weighted as 38%. Exams are incredibly difficult. He does not actually teach the material, just works out problems from previous tests. He has the worst averages compared to other profs. Seriously- avoid this man at all costs. Don't waste your time and money.
His lectures are useless, I passed exclusively due to Tatiana's recitation videos.
DONT TAKE HIM!!!!!
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr.Wenhao has been a very difficult professor to work with. The lectures are completely useless, he doesn't like when we ask questions, he accused me of not taking an exam at all and gave a 0 for it. Would definitely try to take another professor if I were you. Practice exams are given and helpful for studying.

There were curves at the end of the semester, pretty generous ones at that. We had a weird semester because of his family emergencies and a few technical difficulties. Other than that, it is a class where you teach yourself. I personally find his lectures counterproductive as he teaches how to solve the problems instead of the actual concepts.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The homework are quite difficult despite being what this class is, final exam weighs heavily. He doesn't really really teach the concepts but rather how to do the exam. But if you relying on memorizing the exams then you don't really understand the subject and it will throw you off when the actual exam is different from the mock (which is the case)

Hw website is useless for learning and adds more stress. Buy chegg to avoid the stress. Class lectures are hard to understand and he goes through content like we should already know what to do. Lecture slides are crammed and work shown is not neat or in order. Lab will help you since its online and recitation can be helpful if youre lucky.

No physics teacher is great but if you'e looking to pass, understand how to do the practice exams and you should be fine. If you need to learn this material, search up AK lectures or learn from the recitation leaders. Found Wu's lectures super boring, hard to understand, and only gave examples during reviews which are luckily from practice exams.

This was his first semester teaching 202 and it was so hard. The exams, though they looked similar to the past exams, included questions that we had never seen before or never gone over. Lectures were hard to follow and I had to learn from my recitation leader. Take someone else

Professor Wu went through the notes every lecture, operating under the assumption that students knew what they were doing. His work was unclear and his inability to explain concepts entailed difficulties. Also, the homework assignments almost never resembled test questions or what was in the notes. His class is not worth the stress.
Very hard to understand and does not teach what you need to know for the test.
I would say skip class, you wont pass, but the lectures are so hard to follow it doesnt really matter. SI sessions and even a separate tutor might be required to prepare for the tests.

attendance not mandatory but quizzes each class. go to the SI sessions if you can't get a different prof. i treated the SI's as the lectures. for studying, try to redo the SI problems on your own and go through all of the practice tests. practice problems are key to subjects like physics. usually a pretty big curve. at midterm, 80 to 100 was an A.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Honestly, I didn't listen to any of his lectures. Just do the homeworks, and take the common exams. The homework is a lot more difficult than the exams. If you took physics and high school and did well, you will probably do fine in his class. But if you need to learn at all, take someone else.

He seems like a nice guy outside of class, but he assigns way too much homework. Also blames students and called us all lazy when the class average was a 50 on one of the tests. He also teaches units that aren't on the next test before you take the test, so the last few lectures' material doesn't appear on the test. Really not a fun guy.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The worst prof I've had. Doesn't care about his students, treats you like your an idiot if you ask questions, hard to understand. Asks if anyone has questions in class but wont turn around even though there is 10 hands up. Rude in office hours, honestly don't know why we let people that act like this teach here. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.ratingTags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: PHYS206 is a tough course on its own. That said, this prof didn't help. The lectures were really hard to follow along with, examples were given but not really explained, the answers were just posted on the slides without an explanation on how they got there. Only went to class because of clickers, otherwise I would've skipped bc it didn't help.

His lectures weren't helpful at all the Hw system sucks, and most likely you will have to lean the stuff yourslef. the only reson people show up for his class is there is in class quiz. He does care but that does not make the class easier.

His lectures weren't the best due to language barrier and his accent. But I did find that if I went back over his lectures by myself they made more sense. There wasn't really anything bad or good about him, just a pretty average professor. The test system is weird so make sure you understand it.

University physics is definitely tough no matter who you have. It is definitely a possible class but you're most likely going to be teaching yourself. Wu loves physics but his lectures are him just potting up a slide and using a pointer the whole time to read from it. He took attendance via clicker questions but nobody ever got them correct!

Wu is not a good teacher in either the lecture or in office hours. He cares about the subject but the lectures are next to pointless. Textbook is only slightly helpful for the homeworks but otherwise with Wu the class is a trainwreck. Pray you can get a decent TA who actually teaches the material in a comprehensive manner during recitations.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: If you are taking UP physics, just get ready to get screwed either way. As far as professor Wu goes, he is a caring person, you can tell he loves physics, but he cannot teach it for the life of him. He reads off the power points directly, there is very little explanation of topic. I would take someone else. I love physics, but this class-tested me.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures ar'nt mandatory, but there are clicker questions that count towards your grade so they are mandatory. My grade got better once I stopped going to class. He never makes hw due by midnight its always at a weird time and does not tell us. Our class was so behind that out TA for recitation had to teach us. Even my TA hates his teaching.

Better get ready to teach yourself, you will rely heavily on SI's and tutors (or at least I did). I showed up to lecture but just to sit there and do homework. For exams, if you do practice tests from the past and can understand what your doing you will do fine but you definitely will have to work for a B and above. Take Ford if you have the option
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Super nice guy, but I never got a lot out of lecture and his examples could be hard to understand because he never completely work through the problems. I learned material through A plus and SI.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Wu is a nice guy, but not a great professor. SI sessions were what got me through. Professor Wu's in-class reviews the day before exams were pretty much the only useful lectures. He also has a heavy accent that can be difficult to understand. I had to put a lot of time in outside of class to do well.

I took Wu because PHYS 201 was required for my major. He doesn't really explain and convey the information that needed to be taught well. Rely HEAVILY on SI sessions and outside tutoring. Great guy, not a great professor. Has a heavy accent. Only went to class to get tests back.

Not good at explaining- he teaches as if you've already memorized the exam equations sheet. Will round up to next letter grade if you have >.5% (ex: 79.5% -> 80%). Otherwise, no chance. Expect to get 68% of the clicker portion of your grade. Recitation grade varys on TA, I recommend to just attend every class. I got As and Bs in all other classes
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Really accessible outside of class. Physics sucks regardless, so at least hes nice. Reads from powerpoints that are copies of the textbook. If you can take physics somewhere else, do it.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: awesome1!!1!1!1!! :D rawr xD

His lectures are terrible & confused me even more than just reading the book and figuring out the homework. He just read from the slides & his "examples" are just pre-worked out/typed problems that don't show/explain all his steps. He knows what he is talking about but cannot teach, so you have to teach yourself, which seems to be a theme of 218.

PHYS218 is a pain no matter how you take it, mostly due to the grading structure. If possible, just accept your AP credit or take the class online. It's not worth all the work to only end up with a C or B... Wenhao is a nice person, and if you go to his office hours, he sometimes gives back points on exams (as long as there is a good reason).

Wu knows what he's talking about, but has a REALLY hard time teaching it. I went to class for iClicker questions then did online homework during class because his lectures made me more confused than trying to learn it on my own. I went to tutoring for every test and that helped a lot. I took him Spring 2017 and tests were just like Ford's old ones.

He knows his stuff. But he doesn't translate it well. Slides are just from the book. He doesn't give a lot of examples just 1 or 2 per section. "Pop quiz" are clicker questions. A good amount of homework that can get pretty hard. Tests aren't too bad if you review the past exams. The mid terms are in the somewhat same format as the past exams.
reviews.ratingTags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: I took Professor Wu for PHYS 201, and in lecture he wasnt that helpful. He talked more concept than actual problems, so when you get to the homework you arent really prepared becuase he never did an example. He posts his lecture slides, but he doesnt show the simplifications he does to the equations, making the formulas hard to follow. Get a tutor

Dr. Wu is awesome! He genuinely wants everyone to learn and do well in his class. He is always willing to help and super knowledgeable about Physics. There's a lot of homework, but to my knowledge that is pretty standard for Phys201. He gives you a lot of tools to study and is an overall incredible professor. I highly recommend his class.

Physics in general is going to be hard regardless who you take. However, Wu doesn't assign hw and just expects you to learn from the book. Personally, his lectures weren't as helpful and the only way to be successful is to practice from either the book and old practice tests. Definitely recommend office hours and going to SI.

Dr. Wu seems to be more of a researcher than a professor, but he's very knowledgeable and passionate about physics.  He's very nice and helpful in his office. I found an exam grading error and he immediately changed my grade. His accent is understandable. The textbook is pretty useful. Working past exams is the best way to study for 218 tests.

He was a good professor, always willing to work with you. He was willing to flex his office hours for you if you asked. Anything that wasn't clear in lecture, he would clarify in office hours. Very nice fellow.

Doctor Wu is a terrible teacher in general, when he tries to explain things its not only hard to understand but not helpful to the subject he is trying to teach. He is very excited about the  material, but cannot explain it for the life of him. If you are taking his course the book will be the only thing you will learn from and youtube, good luck.

I struggled in this class but that's because mechanics in general is pretty tough. I always attended his office hours and he was always willing to help. He's a great professor and I don't think his accent is bad at all. The textbook is a must have! READ IT AND DO PRACTICE PROBLEMS BEFORE GOING TO LECTURE.

He's a little tough to understand at times, but he doesn't assign any homework and  he will help you the best he can as long as you ask for it. Also he does quizzes every lecture to take attendance, not a huge part of your grade but if you are border line the quizzes may help.
